newsitem.title: UK: UK unions set out agenda for Sept annual meeting.
newsitem.headline: UK unions set out agenda for Sept annual meeting.

text.p: The main campaigning body for British unions published on Wednesday the agenda for its annual meeting on September 8-11, the first under the new Labour government.

Prime Minister Tony Blair will address the Trades Union Congress (TUC) meeting, which is taking as its theme the idea of social partnership between unions, government and big business, the TUC said in a statement.

Observers said the meeting was likely to fire debate among union delegates and Labour party members about the future role of unions in Britain and the need for improvements to employment law and conditions.
Blair will be the first Labour prime minister to attend the conference since James Callaghan in 1978.
Last year, a leaked comment by a Labour party spokesman that Labour was considering cutting its links with the unions enraged many attending the conference.

In addition to government representatives, the Archbishop of Canterbury George Carey, Confederation of British Industry director general Adair Turner and Pauline Green, leader of the Socialist Group in the European Parliament, will be among the speakers.

The congress will also discuss and propose motions on employment rights, criminal justice, employment and the economy, and education and employment, as well as a raft of other political and social issues.

The TUC said it would be publishing its annual report and summary of activities, which would also be available on its website for the first time. The General Council Report to Congress will be on http://www.tuc.org.uk
